recall_prompt: Say how you would work this out — say what you do before pairing anything, and what parts (i) and (iii) should have in common.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Work out the brackets, then parts (i) and (ii)
steps.margin_note: First mark. The union and the intersection inside the brackets are done before any pairing. The counts are 3 × 4 = 12 pairs in (i) and 3 × 1 = 3 pairs in (ii).

recall.must_convey: That B ∪ C and B ∩ C are found first, then each is paired with A, giving 12 pairs and 3 pairs.
accept: do the bracket first then multiply by A
B union C is four five six seven and B intersection C is just five
twelve pairs in part one and three pairs in part two
modata bracket lo unnadi cheyyali taruvata A tho pair cheyyali
three times four is twelve pairs

steps.why: The bracket is a set operation and the product comes after it, so B ∪ C and B ∩ C must be written down first. The counts 12 and 3 tell you at once whether a pair has been missed.
steps.memory_tip: The number of pairs is the number of elements in the first set times the number in the second.
common_mistakes: Pairing A with B and with C separately in part (i), which is part (iii) instead.
Writing the pairs as (4, 2) with the entry from A second.

steps.label: Work out part (iii) and compare with (i)
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The pairs (2,5), (3,5) and (4,5) are in both products, so they are written once in the union. The result must match part (i) exactly.
lines: Join the two, writing each pair once:

recall.must_convey: That A × B and A × C are joined, repeats written once, and the result equals part (i).
accept: work A cross B and A cross C then take their union
the three pairs with five in them appear in both so write them once
part three comes out the same as part one
rendintini kalipithe part one lo vachina answer ye vasthundi
twelve pairs again matching the first part

steps.why: Parts (i) and (iii) coming out equal is the point of the question: it shows the Cartesian product distributes over a union, the same way multiplication distributes over addition.
steps.memory_tip: A × (B ∪ C) = (A × B) ∪ (A × C) — the product distributes over the union, the same way multiplication distributes over addition.
common_mistakes: Listing (2,5), (3,5) and (4,5) twice, once from each product.
Stopping after A × B and A × C without taking their union.
Getting 15 pairs by adding the two counts 6 + 9 instead of removing the repeats.
